states.name: Goa

states.name: Karnataka
states.description: Home to Vijayanagara empire ruins, Hoysala stone temples, and Silicon Valley innovations.

states.name: Telangana
states.description: The realm of the Nizams, pearl bazaars, and colossal medieval granite citadels.

states.name: West Bengal

states.name: Punjab
states.description: Land of five rivers, heroic heritage, spiritual devotion, and warm agricultural bounty.

states.description: Paradise on Earth with serene Alpine lakes, Mughal gardens, and snow-capped Himalayan peaks.

states.name: Sikkim
states.description: Himalayan Buddhist sanctum surrounded by Kanchenjunga peaks and ancient monasteries.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.description: The City of Dreams, financial capital, and gateway to Western India heritage.

cities.name: Pune
cities.description: Cultural capital of Maharashtra with historic Maratha citadels and palace museums.

cities.name: Jaipur
cities.description: The Pink City, showcasing royal Rajput forts, celestial observatories, and palaces.

cities.name: Udaipur
cities.description: City of Lakes, renowned for romantic marble palaces and lakeside ghats.

cities.name: New Delhi
cities.description: Historic national capital filled with UNESCO World Heritage monuments.

cities.name: Agra
cities.description: Home to the iconic Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and imperial Mughal architecture.

cities.name: Varanasi
cities.description: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities on the sacred banks of the Ganges.

cities.name: Kochi
cities.description: Historic spice trading port blending Portuguese, Dutch, British, and indigenous culture.

cities.name: Munnar
cities.description: Serene hill station enveloped by rolling tea plantations and mist-covered valleys.

cities.name: Panaji & Coastal Goa
cities.description: Charming colonial Latin quarters, 16th-century cathedrals, and coastal defense forts.

cities.name: Bengaluru
cities.description: The Garden City and technology hub, with Tudor-style palaces and sprawling botanical gardens.

cities.name: Hampi
cities.description: UNESCO World Heritage boulder-strewn landscape with grand 14th-century Vijayanagara ruins.

cities.name: Hyderabad
cities.description: City of Pearls, famous for Charminar, Golconda Fort acoustic marvels, and royal cuisine.

cities.name: Kolkata
cities.description: City of Joy, featuring grand colonial architecture, vibrant tramways, and historic river ghats.

cities.name: Amritsar
cities.description: Spiritual sanctum of the Sikh faith with the magnificent Golden Temple and sacred sarovar.

cities.name: Srinagar
cities.description: Jewel of Kashmir with Dal Lake shikaras, floating gardens, and royal Mughal terraces.

cities.name: Gangtok
cities.description: Pristine Himalayan town offering breathtaking views of Mt. Kanchenjunga and monasteries.

cities.name: Santiniketan
cities.description: UNESCO World Heritage cultural town established by Rabindranath Tagore, home to Visva-Bharati University.

cities.name: Siliguri
cities.description: Gateway city to the North East and foothills of the Himalayas, known for Dooars wildlife and national parks.

cities.name: Darjeeling
cities.description: Queen of the Hills, famous for the UNESCO Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, tea gardens, and Kanchenjunga sunrise views.

places.name: Gateway of India
places.description: An iconic 26-meter basalt arch monument erected to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911. Overlooking the Arabian Sea, it represents Indo-Saracenic architecture with intricate Gujarati latticework.
places.short_description: Iconic 26m basalt arch monument facing Mumbai Harbour.
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Early morning or sunset)

places.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
places.description: An outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India, blended with themes deriving from Indian traditional architecture. Designed by Frederick William Stevens and completed in 1888.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage Victorian Gothic railway headquarters.
places.best_time_to_visit: All year round (Evenings for exterior architectural illumination)

places.name: Elephanta Caves
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave temples dating from 5th to 7th century AD dedicated to Lord Shiva, featuring the monumental 20-foot high Trimurti sculpture portraying Sadashiva.
places.short_description: Ancient UNESCO rock-cut cave temples on Gharapuri Island.
places.address: Gharapuri Island, Raigad District (Ferry from Gateway of India), Maharashtra 400001
places.best_time_to_visit: November to March (Ferry closed during heavy monsoon)

opening_hours.monday: Closed

accessibility_info.notes: Steps leading up the hill; palanquin (doli) service available for elderly.

places.name: Kanheri Caves
places.description: A group of 109 Buddhist rock-cut monuments chiselled out of massive basaltic rock inside the lush forests of Sanjay Gandhi National Park, dating from 1st century BCE to 10th century CE.
places.short_description: 109 rock-cut Buddhist caves inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park.
places.address: Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Borivali East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400066
places.historical_period: Maurya to Rashtrakuta Period (1st BCE–10th CE)
places.best_time_to_visit: July to February (Monsoon reveals cascading waterfalls)

opening_hours.monday: Closed

accessibility_info.notes: Forest trails and carved stone steps.

places.name: Shree Siddhivinayak Temple
places.description: Historic Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha, consecrated in 1801. Known for its gold-plated sanctum dome and revered as one of the richest and most visited pilgrimage sites in India.
places.short_description: Revered 19th-century Ganesha temple in Prabhadevi.
places.address: SK Bole Marg, Prabhadevi, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400028
places.best_time_to_visit: All year round (Early morning 06:00 to avoid queues)

accessibility_info.notes: Special priority queues and wheelchair access ramps available.

places.name: Shaniwar Wada
places.description: Historical 7-storey stone fortified palace of the Maratha Peshwas built in 1732 by Peshwa Baji Rao I. Famous for the massive Dilli Darwaza with iron spikes and scenic fountain gardens.
places.short_description: 18th-century Maratha Peshwa fortification and seat of power.
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Evenings for light & sound show)

accessibility_info.notes: Paved courtyard accessible via ground level ramp.

places.name: Aga Khan Palace
places.description: Majestic Italian-arched palace built in 1892 by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III. Served as the prison for Mahatma Gandhi, Kasturba Gandhi, and Sarojini Naidu during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
places.short_description: Italianate palace museum closely tied to India's freedom struggle.
places.address: Nagar Road, Samrat Ashok Nagar, Kalyani Nagar, Pune, Maharashtra 411006

accessibility_info.notes: Spacious gardens with flat asphalt walking paths.

places.name: Sinhagad Fort
places.description: Hill fortress located 30 km southwest of Pune perched at 1,312 meters above sea level. Site of the legendary 1670 Battle of Sinhagad fought by Tanaji Malusare.
places.short_description: Historic Sahyadri mountain citadel offering panoramic valley views.
places.unesco_status: Part of Serial Nomination of Maratha Military Landscapes
places.best_time_to_visit: June to February (Monsoon brings mist and waterfalls)

accessibility_info.notes: Rugged hill terrain; trekking pathway.

places.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
places.description: Five-storey pink and red sandstone palace built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh. Features 953 intricately carved jharokhas (small casements) designed like Lord Krishna's crown to allow royal women to observe street festivals unseen.
places.short_description: Iconic 1799 pink sandstone facade with 953 lattice windows.
places.address: Hawa Mahal Rd, Badi Choupad, J.D.A. Market, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302002
places.heritage_status: State Protected Monument / UNESCO Jaipur City Ensemble
places.unesco_status: Part of Jaipur Walled City UNESCO Site (2019)
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Morning sun enhances the sandstone hues)

accessibility_info.notes: Ramps inside upper floors instead of stairs, but entry has steps.

places.name: Amber Fort & Palace
places.description: Massive hill fort crafted from yellow and pink sandstone and white marble. Highlights include the Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), Diwan-e-Aam, and panoramic views of Maota Lake.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage hilltop palace with shimmering mirror hall.
places.heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Early morning or evening sound & light show)

accessibility_info.notes: Jeep / battery operated vehicle shuttle available to top courtyards.

places.name: City Palace Jaipur
places.description: A magnificent royal complex blending Rajput, Mughal, and European architectural styles. Established in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, featuring the Chandra Mahal, Mubarak Mahal, and museum galleries.
places.short_description: Regal complex with peacock courtyards, armouries, and royal museums.
places.address: Tulsi Marg, Gangori Bazaar, J.D.A. Market, Pink City, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302002

accessibility_info.notes: Wheelchair ramps throughout the main courtyards.

places.name: Jantar Mantar Observatory
places.description: Collection of nineteen architectural astronomical instruments built by the Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh II and completed in 1734. Features the world's largest stone sundial, the Vrihat Samrat Yantra.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage 18th-century stone astronomical observatory.
places.address: Gangori Bazaar, J.D.A. Market, Pink City, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302002
places.best_time_to_visit: Midday (To observe solar shadow movements on astronomical dials)

accessibility_info.notes: Flat stone paved pathways connecting all major instruments.

places.name: City Palace Udaipur
places.description: Colossal lakeside palace complex built over nearly 400 years by the rulers of the Mewar dynasty on the eastern banks of Lake Pichola. Notable for its ornate balconies, mirror mosaics, and vintage crystal gallery.
places.short_description: Grand 400-year-old Mewar dynasty marble palace on Lake Pichola.

accessibility_info.notes: Multiple levels with historic stone steps; ground courtyards accessible.

places.name: Lake Pichola & Jag Mandir
places.description: An artificial freshwater lake created in the year 1362 AD. Features island palaces including the Lake Palace (Taj Lake Palace) and Jag Mandir, set against the backdrop of the Aravalli hills.
places.short_description: Scenic 14th-century freshwater lake surrounded by royal marble palaces.
places.address: Rameshwar Ghat, City Palace Complex, Udaipur, Rajasthan 313001

accessibility_info.notes: Boats have ramp access from City Palace jetty.

places.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
places.description: Historic red sandstone fortress constructed in 1639 by the fifth Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as the palace of his fortified capital Shahjahanabad. Known for its massive ramparts, Lahori Gate, and the Diwan-i-Khas.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage Mughal imperial palace citadel in Old Delhi.
places.address: Netaji Subhash Marg, Lal Qila, Chandni Chowk, New Delhi, Delhi 110006
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Mornings or evening sound & light)

opening_hours.monday: Closed

accessibility_info.notes: Electric golf carts available from outer entrance to main gate.

places.name: Qutub Minar & Complex
places.description: A 72.5-meter tapering fluted red sandstone minaret built in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak. The complex contains the ancient 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II and Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque.
places.short_description: World's tallest brick minaret and UNESCO medieval monument complex.
places.address: Seth Sarai, Mehrauli, New Delhi, Delhi 110030

accessibility_info.notes: Paved pathways surround all major ruins in the garden complex.

places.name: Humayun's Tomb
places.description: Splendid garden tomb built in 1570 by Empress Bega Begum for Mughal Emperor Humayun. Regarded as the architectural precursor and inspiration for the Taj Mahal, surrounded by formal Persian Charbagh gardens.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage Mughal garden tomb and precursor to the Taj Mahal.
places.address: Mathura Rd, Nizamuddin East, New Delhi, Delhi 110013

accessibility_info.notes: Ramps lead up to the plinth; gardens are universally accessible.

places.source: ASI / Aga Khan Trust for Culture

places.name: India Gate & Kartavya Path
places.description: A 42-meter high triumphal arch war memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1931. Commemorates 84,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army who fell during World War I and Anglo-Afghan wars.
places.short_description: National triumphal arch memorial and ceremonial avenue.
places.address: Kartavya Path, India Gate, New Delhi, Delhi 110001

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.description: An immense ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river, commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan for his favorite wife Mumtaz Mahal. A universal jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the New 7 Wonders of the World.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece and New 7 Wonder of the World.
places.address: Dharmapuri, Forest Colony, Tajganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282001
places.heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983) / New 7 Wonder
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Sunrise for soft pink and golden hues)

opening_hours.friday: Closed

accessibility_info.notes: Electric vehicles transport visitors from parking; ramps available to plinth.

places.name: Agra Fort
places.description: Historical 16th-century fortress of red sandstone in the city of Agra. Served as the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal Dynasty until 1638. Highlights include Jahangiri Mahal, Khas Mahal, and Musamman Burj.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage red sandstone citadel of Mughal emperors.
places.address: Agra Fort, Rakabganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282003

accessibility_info.notes: Ramps available through Amar Singh Gate to courtyards.

places.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple & Corridor
places.description: One of the most sacred Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, home to the sacred Jyotirlinga of Vishweshwara. Rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar in 1780 and newly expanded via the Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor.
places.short_description: Holiest Jyotirlinga shrine on the banks of the sacred Ganges River.
places.unesco_status: Part of Varanasi Heritage Tentative List
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Mangala Aarti at 03:00 or evening)

accessibility_info.notes: New corridor features escalators, travelators, and smooth granite ramps from ghats.

places.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat (Ganga Aarti)
places.description: The main and most historic ghat on the Ganga river in Varanasi. Famous worldwide for the synchronized evening Maha Ganga Aarti performed with brass lamps, conch shells, and incense by priests.
places.short_description: Ancient sacred river ghat celebrated for the evening Ganga Aarti.
places.address: Dashashwamedh Ghat Rd, Bangali Tola, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh 221001
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (18:00 for the Grand Evening Aarti)

places.name: Fort Kochi & Chinese Fishing Nets
places.description: Cantilevered shore-operated fishing lift nets established by Chinese traders in the 14th century, set along the historic colonial promenade of Fort Kochi featuring St. Francis Church and Vasco House.
places.short_description: 14th-century cantilevered fishing nets and historic colonial port.
places.address: River Rd, Fort Kochi, Kochi, Kerala 682001

places.name: Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace)
places.description: Portuguese-built palace gifted to the King of Cochin in 1555 and later renovated by the Dutch. Renowned for its extraordinary murals depicting scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata in tempera technique.
places.short_description: 16th-century palace museum famous for classical Hindu mythological murals.

opening_hours.monday: Closed
opening_hours.friday: Closed

accessibility_info.notes: Wooden staircase leading to first floor museum exhibits.

places.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage 16th-century Catholic basilica in Old Goa housing the sacred mortal remains of Saint Francis Xavier. Exemplifies Portuguese Baroque architecture with carved basaltic embellishments.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage Baroque basilica in Old Goa holding St. Francis Xavier relic.

accessibility_info.notes: Ramp available at side entrance into the nave.

places.name: Fort Aguada & Lighthouse
places.description: Well-preserved 17th-century Portuguese fortress and 4-storey lighthouse standing on Sinquerim Beach overlooking the confluence of Mandovi River and Arabian Sea. Constructed in 1612 to protect against Dutch fleets.
places.short_description: 1612 Portuguese coastal fort with freshwater springs and panoramic lighthouse.
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Late afternoon for sea breeze)

accessibility_info.notes: Lower fort and museum ramp-equipped; upper ramparts have stone inclines.

places.name: Bangalore Palace
places.description: Grand royal palace constructed in Tudor Revival style with fortified towers, battlements, and turreted battlements by Rev. J. Garrett in 1878, later purchased by the Wadiyar dynasty Maharajas of Mysore.
places.short_description: Tudor-style royal palace with wooden carvings and manicured lawns.

accessibility_info.notes: Ground floor accessible via ramp.

places.name: Virupaksha Temple & Hampi Bazaar
places.description: Part of the Group of Monuments at Hampi UNESCO site on the banks of Tungabhadra River. Dedicated to Lord Virupaksha (Shiva), active continuously since the 7th century through the golden age of the Vijayanagara Empire.
places.short_description: UNESCO World Heritage 7th-century Dravidian temple complex in Vijayanagara.

accessibility_info.notes: Flat stone floor courtyards.

places.name: Vittala Temple & Stone Chariot
places.description: Architectural marvel of the Vijayanagara empire, featuring the iconic monolithic granite Stone Chariot dedicated to Garuda (depicted on the ₹50 banknote) and musical stone pillars in the Ranga Mandapa.
places.short_description: World-famous monolithic granite stone chariot and musical pillar mandapa.
places.best_time_to_visit: October to February (Early morning or sunset)

accessibility_info.notes: Electric buggy transport connects parking area to temple gates.

places.name: Charminar
places.description: Monument and mosque built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to commemorate the eradication of plague. Its four grand arches open into the lively Laad Bazaar and Mecca Masjid.
places.short_description: 1591 landmark four-minaret square gateway in old Hyderabad.
places.address: Char Kaman, Ghansi Bazaar, Hyderabad, Telangana 500002

accessibility_info.notes: Surrounding pedestrianized plaza is fully accessible.

places.name: Golconda Fort
places.description: Colossal fortified citadel famous for its ingenious acoustic engineering, diamond vault mines (which produced the Koh-i-Noor and Hope Diamond), and royal palaces.
places.short_description: Massive granite fortress renowned for acoustic marvels and diamond vaults.
places.unesco_status: Tentative List (Monuments of the Qutb Shahi Sultanate)
places.best_time_to_visit: October to March (Late afternoon or sound & light show)

accessibility_info.notes: Lower entrance gate accessible; steep uphill climb to Bala Hissar pavilion.

places.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
places.description: Pre-eminent spiritual shrine of Sikhism, covered in real gold leaf and surrounded by the sacred Amrit Sarovar lake. Famous for serving free communal meals to over 100,000 pilgrims daily in the world's largest community kitchen (Langar).
places.short_description: Holiest gold-plated Sikh sanctum surrounded by the sacred Amrit Sarovar.
places.address: Golden Temple Rd, Atta Mandi, Amritsar, Punjab 143006
places.best_time_to_visit: All year round (04:00 for Palki Sahib ceremony or evening illumination)

places.name: Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial
places.description: Historic public garden and sacred national memorial commemorating peaceful protestors massacred under British colonial rule on 13 April 1919. Contains the preserved Martyrs' Well, bullet marks in brick walls, and the eternal flame.
places.short_description: Solemn national memorial of India's freedom struggle.

accessibility_info.notes: Paved memorial walkway throughout.

places.name: Dal Lake & Shikara Promenade
places.description: Iconic urban lake in Srinagar, known as the 'Jewel in the crown of Kashmir'. Famous for ornate carved wooden houseboats, vibrant floating vegetable markets, and traditional shikara boat rides against the Pir Panjal mountains.
places.short_description: Scenic Himalayan lake famous for houseboats and shikara rides.
places.address: Boulevard Rd, Dal Lake, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir 190001
places.best_time_to_visit: April to October (Spring tulip bloom to autumn chinar leaves)

accessibility_info.notes: Boulevard road has wide accessible pavement; ghat boarding requires manual aid.

places.name: Shalimar Bagh Mughal Garden
places.description: Renowned terraced Mughal garden laid out in 1619 by Emperor Jahangir for his wife Nur Jahan. Linked to Dal Lake via a canal, featuring cascading water fountains, chinar trees, and black marble pavilion pillars.
places.short_description: 1619 imperial Mughal terraced garden with water cascades and ancient chinars.
places.heritage_status: UNESCO Tentative List (Mughal Gardens of Kashmir)

accessibility_info.notes: Stone terraced pathways with ramp connections.

places.name: Rumtek Monastery (Dharma Chakra Centre)
places.description: Focal seat of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism in exile, located 24 km from Gangtok. Features traditional Tibetan murals, golden stupas, precious silk thangkas, and monastic chanting halls.
places.short_description: Premier Kagyu Tibetan Buddhist monastery and golden stupa shrine.
places.address: Tsurphu Labrang Pal Karmae Sangha E-Wam Chokhorling, Rumtek, Sikkim 737135
places.best_time_to_visit: March to May & October to December

accessibility_info.notes: Gentle uphill road leads to entrance gate; main prayer hall has steps.

places.name: Tsomgo Lake (Changu Lake)
places.description: Glacial high-altitude alpine lake located at an elevation of 3,753 meters (12,313 ft) on the Gangtok-Nathu La highway. Revered as sacred by indigenous Sikkimese people, reflecting snow-capped peaks in pristine turquoise waters.
places.short_description: Sacred turquoise glacial lake at 3,753m elevation in the East Himalayas.
places.best_time_to_visit: October to December & April to May (Winter brings frozen snowscapes)

accessibility_info.notes: Ropeway cable car available; high altitude requires acclimatization.

places.name: Sarnath Buddhist Complex & Dhamek Stupa
places.description: Sacred pilgrimage site where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta) to his five disciples after attaining enlightenment. Features the imposing 43.6m high Dhamek Stupa and Ashoka Lion Capital.
places.short_description: Site of Buddha’s first sermon, featuring the historic Dhamek Stupa.

places.name: Assi Ghat & Subah-e-Banaras
places.description: The southernmost and most culturally vibrant ghat of Varanasi at the confluence of the Ganga and Assi rivers. Renowned for dawn Vedic rituals, classical morning ragas, and spiritual meditation.
places.short_description: Southernmost major ghat celebrated for dawn cultural and spiritual gatherings.
places.address: Assi Ghat, Shivala, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh 221005

places.name: Mehtab Bagh (Moonlight Garden)
places.description: Charbagh garden complex situated on the opposite bank of the Yamuna River, perfectly aligned with the Taj Mahal. Offers the iconic postcard sunset view of the Taj Mahal reflecting in the river.
places.short_description: Mughal riverfront garden offering iconic reflections of the Taj Mahal.
places.address: Dharmapuri, Forest Colony, Tajganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282001

places.name: Tipu Sultan’s Summer Palace
places.description: An exquisite example of Indo-Islamic teakwood architecture built within the walls of Bangalore Fort. Completed during Tipu Sultan’s reign in 1791, adorned with ornamental frescoes, teak pillars, and cusped arches.
places.short_description: Intricate two-storey teakwood summer residence of the Mysore Kingdom.
places.address: Albert Victor Rd, Chamrajpet, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560018

places.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden & Heritage Glass House
places.description: Historic 240-acre botanical haven commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760. Features the majestic 1889 cast-iron Glass House inspired by London’s Crystal Palace and a 3,000-million-year-old Peninsular Gneiss rock formation.
places.short_description: Centuries-old botanical sanctuary centered on the Victorian cast-iron Glass House.

places.name: The Partition Museum (Town Hall)
places.description: World’s first museum dedicated to the memory of the 1947 Partition of India. Housed in the red-brick colonial Town Hall, displaying oral histories, personal artifacts, archival documents, and multimedia memoirs.
places.short_description: Profound historical repository chronicling the 1947 Partition of the subcontinent.
places.address: Town Hall, Katra Ahluwalia, Amritsar, Punjab 143006

places.name: Victoria Memorial
places.description: A grand marble monument and museum built in memory of Queen Victoria, surrounded by gardens.
places.short_description: A grand marble monument and museum built in memory of Queen Victoria, surrounded by gardens.
